text: Databases store and organise information so we can find it easily. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases use tables with rows and columns, while NoSQL databases store data in flexible forms like documents. To get information, we write queries, which are special commands that ask the database questions. Before building a database, we create a data model to plan how the data connects. We also add indexes, which work like a book's index and help the database find data much faster. Choosing the right type and design makes a big difference.
